To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spatial density of glutamateric synapses on the arbors of retinal ganglions cells varies little within an arbor, that the total density of synaptic contacts on the arbors scales inversely with the arbor area, and that the distribution of excitator inputs is concentrated around a ring‐shapd region of the soma.

The spatial pattern of glutamateric input to retinal ganglion cell dendrites is remarkably similar across a wide range of cell types, and the density of synaptic inputs varies inversely with the area of the dendrites, so that narrow arbors receive more synaptic input per unit area.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial pattern of excitory synaptic input in the retina is remarkably similar across all cell types and sizes.
the density of excitatory input to retinal ganglion cell dendrites is uniform, and that this is consistent with the functional requirements of the cell.
the spatial distribution of excitatory input to retinal ganglion cell dendrites follows a single set of scaling laws that is independent of cell size, morphology, or function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the density of excitatory synaptic input onto dendrites of retinogeniculate ganglion cells is surprisingly uniform, and that this is true for a wide variety of ganglion cell morphologies.

the distribution of synaptic inputs to retinal ganglion cell arbors is remarkably uniform, despite wide variation in the morphology of the cells, their receptive fields, and their functional properties.
